questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Limerick had the relevant courses I needed to take, and I always wanted to go to Ireland to see the beautiful nature and experience their culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: no

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Great! University of Limerick were very welcoming and it was easy to get the help I needed. With one exception though: I didn't get student accommodation and it was difficult and frustrating to find a place to stay. I wish the University would have warned me at how difficult accommodation would be.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help with documents

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think the welcoming programme needed more social activities, and it was very much suited to the students who lived on campus, and not the students who lived off campus.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Start very early in searching. Also you aren't guaranteed that you will receive student accomodation, so be prepared for that.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very pricy, and there is a lot of people taking advantage of the housing crisis, which means you should lower your expectations to distance to the university and the general state of condition that you will be staying in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The University shouldn't accept that many international students when there is such an issue getting housing off campus, and they can't provide accomodation to all incoming international students. Even though I recognize that generally it isn't the responsibility of the University, it is especially difficult in Ireland to find a place to stay, so they should recognize that this is a real issue for incoming students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was difficult to get help, and difficult to get responses from my host university. It took an unecessary long time to get a response to whether my chosen courses would be approved or not, which really was what determined whether I would be able to go abroad.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be very prepared before you apply, that you have confidence that you will be able to get your chosen courses approved.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did my 5th semester of my bachelor abroad

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was great. Much more personal with the teachers, and much more guidance in the writing of the mandatory essays. Also they were great at giving feedback at the midterms which really improved my strategies for the finals

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Gender and Popular Culture
Russian Politics
Nationalism, Ethnicity and Conflict
Policy-making in the European Union
Comparative European Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociology of Gender and Popular Culture. The teacher Carmen Kuhling was really great, and it held a very high level academically.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to relocate, and I lost some money at the first place I stayed at. Also 200 euros on heating was an additional cost I didn't expect

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lost of great options, and the clubs in the University provided tons of opportunities to do outdoor activities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tons of different clubs. Almost anything you could imagine. Really awesome.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did kayaking with the kayak club and it was so much fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go away to all the little irish towns, and do a lot of hiking. So many beautiful places to see and experience wherever you go in Ireland. And also drink a lot of guinness and eat a lot in irish pubs.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs. Generally the students were a bit younger than me, so I mostly hung out with other international students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is kind of hard to get around to cool places by public transport. I can be done, but it is a lot easier if you can get around by car

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pubs, the music, and everything outdoor.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Beware of housing possibilities and housing prices. Join a club. And leave the city and experience the rest of Ireland on the weekends. And also a fourth: don't plan to many visits, because a single semester is quite a short time, and you'll have more opportunities if your weekends are free.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The outdoors and my new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to relocate when I arrived in Limerick, and finding a new place to stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
